/-!
# Polyhedra with more than seven pairwise adjacent faces

The tetrahedron ($4$ faces, genus $0$) and the Szilassi polyhedron ($7$ hexagonal faces,
genus $1$) are the only known polyhedra in which every face shares an edge with every other
face. If a polyhedron with $f$ faces and $h$ holes has this property, then Euler's formula
gives $h \geq (f-4)(f-3)/12$, with equality when each vertex has degree $3$ and each pair of
faces shares exactly one edge. The next candidate is $f = 12$, $h = 6$, and it is not known
whether such a polyhedron can be realised geometrically in $\mathbb{R}^3$ without
self-intersections (rather than as an abstract polytope).

Wikipedia asks: *Is there a non-convex polyhedron without self-intersections with more than
seven faces, all of which share an edge with each other?*

Here a *polyhedron* is a finite set of *faces*, each a planar simple (not necessarily convex)
polygon in $\mathbb{R}^3$, such that two distinct faces meet only along their boundaries, faces
sharing an edge are not coplanar, and the union of the faces is a connected closed surface
(a compact topological $2$-manifold without boundary). The last condition is what "without
self-intersections" means: the surface is embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Two faces *share an edge*
if their intersection contains a line segment of positive length.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Szilassi polyhedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Szilassi_polyhedron)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sz86] Szilassi, L., *Regular toroids*, Structural Topology 13 (1986).
  http://www-iri.upc.es/people/ros/StructuralTopology/ST13/st13-06-a3-ocr.pdf
- [GS09] Grünbaum, B. and Szilassi, L., *Geometric realizations of special toroidal complexes*,
  Contributions to Discrete Mathematics 4 (2009). https://doi.org/10.11575/cdm.v4i1.61986
- [AKKLSVW24] Arseneva, E., Kleist, L., Klemz, B., Löffler, M., Schulz, A., Vogtenhuber, B.
  and Wolff, A., *Adjacency graphs of polyhedral surfaces*, Discrete & Computational Geometry
  (2024). https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-023-00537-6
-/

blocks.name: IsPolyhedron
blocks.text:
/--
A finite set `faces` of subsets of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a *polyhedron without self-intersections*
if
- every face is a planar simple polygon (`IsPolygon`);
- two distinct faces meet only along their boundaries;
- two faces sharing an edge are not coplanar (so faces are genuine faces, not pieces of a
  larger planar face);
- the union of the faces is connected;
- the union of the faces is a topological $2$-manifold without boundary (it is automatically
  compact). Together with the previous conditions this says that the surface is embedded in
  $\mathbb{R}^3$: faces meet only along common edges and vertices, every edge lies in exactly
  two faces, and the faces around each vertex form a single cycle.
-/
structure IsPolyhedron (faces : Finset (Set ℝ³)) : Prop where
  isPolygon : ∀ F ∈ faces, IsPolygon F
  inter_subset_frontier : ∀ F ∈ faces, ∀ G ∈ faces, F ≠ G →
    F ∩ G ⊆ intrinsicFrontier ℝ F ∩ intrinsicFrontier ℝ G
  not_coplanar : ∀ F ∈ faces, ∀ G ∈ faces, F ≠ G → SharesEdge F G →
    ¬ Coplanar ℝ (F ∪ G)
  isConnected : IsConnected (⋃₀ (faces : Set (Set ℝ³)))
  chartedSpace : Nonempty (ChartedSpace ℝ² (⋃₀ (faces : Set (Set ℝ³))))

def IsConvexPolyhedron (faces : Finset (Set ℝ³)) : Prop :=
  ∃ K : Set ℝ³, Convex ℝ K ∧ frontier K = ⋃₀ (faces : Set (Set ℝ³))
blocks.docstring: A polyhedron is *convex* if its surface is the boundary of a convex set.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Convex ℝ` applied to the surface itself (meaningless: a surface is never convex), `frontier (convexHull ℝ S) = S` (equivalent alternative).
justification.name: MoreThanSevenFaces.IsConvexPolyhedron
justification.why_needed: To state the literal 'non-convex' hypothesis: the surface is the boundary of a convex set.

which share an edge with each other?

Here a polyhedron is a finite set of planar simple polygonal faces forming an embedded closed
surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (`IsPolyhedron`), it is convex if its surface bounds a convex set

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no existence question (Prop is `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P, ...`): P must be a genuine embedded (non-self-intersecting, i.e. not merely an abstract polytope or immersed surface) closed polyhedral surface in ℝ³ with planar polygonal faces, strictly more than 7 faces (by the Euler-characteristic relation h=(f-4)(f-3)/12 in the article, any such polyhedron has f ≡ 0,3,4,7 mod 12, so f ≥ 12 and genus ≥ 6, which also makes the 'non-convex' hypothesis automatic rather than an extra constraint), and every pair of distinct faces must share a full common edge (a positive-length segment, not merely a vertex); the article's remark that the f=12, h=6 case (44 vertices, 66 edges) is open is a special case not separately posed by the statement, so it is not listed as its own sub-question.
claims.reviewer_why: c08 models the polyhedron as a Finset of planar simple-polygon faces (coplanar, homeomorphic to a closed disk, relative boundary a finite union of segments) whose union is a connected topological 2-manifold without boundary in ℝ³ (no self-intersections), with distinct faces meeting only along their relative boundaries and edge-adjacent faces required to be non-coplanar (so the face count is intrinsic and cannot be inflated by subdividing a face). 'Share an edge' = intersection contains a positive-length segment (excludes vertex-only contact), face count is strict `7 < faces.card`, non-convexity is kept literally (automatic, hence harmless). Compiles with only the sorry warning. Rejected alternatives: c01 (no non-coplanarity condition for adjacent faces, so coplanar subdivisions could inflate the face count — a permissive relaxation of the intended notion of polyhedron); c02/c03/c05/c06 (require every pair of distinct faces to intersect in EXACTLY one segment, which excludes legitimate polyhedra where two faces share an edge plus a vertex or two edges — an over-restriction not in the source; c02/c03/c05/c06 also lack non-coplanarity); c04 (combinatorial Grünbaum-style definition, also faithful and compiling, but much longer and with more surface for subtle error; c08's set-theoretic model is equivalent in the relevant respects and simpler); c07 (also faithful, with intrinsically defined faces as maximal planar pieces; equivalent to c08 but less explicit). Edit: theorem docstring corrected to say Euler's formula forces positive genus rather than 'genus at least 6' (the latter presupposes exactly one shared edge per pair and trivalent vertices), and a pointer to the bespoke definitions added.

/-!
# Polyhedra with more than seven pairwise adjacent faces

The tetrahedron ($4$ faces, genus $0$) and the Szilassi polyhedron ($7$ hexagonal faces,
genus $1$) are the only known polyhedra in which every face shares an edge with every other

Wikipedia asks: *Is there a non-convex polyhedron without self-intersections with more than

polygon in $\mathbb{R}^3$, such that two distinct faces meet only along their boundaries, faces
sharing an edge are not coplanar, and the union of the faces is a connected closed surface
(a compact topological $2$-manifold without boundary). The last condition is what "without
self-intersections" means: the surface is embedded in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Two faces *share an edge*
if their intersection contains a line segment of positive length.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Szilassi polyhedron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Szilassi_polyhedron)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sz86] Szilassi, L., *Regular toroids*, Structural Topology 13 (1986).
  http://www-iri.upc.es/people/ros/StructuralTopology/ST13/st13-06-a3-ocr.pdf
- [GS09] Grünbaum, B. and Szilassi, L., *Geometric realizations of special toroidal complexes*,
  Contributions to Discrete Mathematics 4 (2009). https://doi.org/10.11575/cdm.v4i1.61986
- [AKKLSVW24] Arseneva, E., Kleist, L., Klemz, B., Löffler, M., Schulz, A., Vogtenhuber, B.
  and Wolff, A., *Adjacency graphs of polyhedral surfaces*, Discrete & Computational Geometry
  (2024). https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-023-00537-6
-/

namespace MoreThanSevenFaces

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/--
A set $F \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is a *polygon* (a simple, not necessarily convex, planar polygon
together with its interior) if it lies in a plane, is homeomorphic to a closed disk, and its
boundary relative to that plane is a finite union of line segments.
-/
def IsPolygon (F : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Coplanar ℝ F ∧
  Nonempty (F ≃ₜ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℝ²) 1) ∧
  ∃ E : Finset (ℝ³ × ℝ³), intrinsicFrontier ℝ F = ⋃ e ∈ E, segment ℝ e.1 e.2

/-- Two faces *share an edge* if their intersection contains a line segment of positive
length (and not merely a vertex). -/
def SharesEdge (F G : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : ℝ³, a ≠ b ∧ segment ℝ a b ⊆ F ∩ G

/--
A finite set `faces` of subsets of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a *polyhedron without self-intersections*
if
- every face is a planar simple polygon (`IsPolygon`);
- two distinct faces meet only along their boundaries;
- two faces sharing an edge are not coplanar (so faces are genuine faces, not pieces of a
  larger planar face);
- the union of the faces is connected;
- the union of the faces is a topological $2$-manifold without boundary (it is automatically
  compact). Together with the previous conditions this says that the surface is embedded in
  $\mathbb{R}^3$: faces meet only along common edges and vertices, every edge lies in exactly
  two faces, and the faces around each vertex form a single cycle.
-/
structure IsPolyhedron (faces : Finset (Set ℝ³)) : Prop where
  isPolygon : ∀ F ∈ faces, IsPolygon F
  inter_subset_frontier : ∀ F ∈ faces, ∀ G ∈ faces, F ≠ G →
    F ∩ G ⊆ intrinsicFrontier ℝ F ∩ intrinsicFrontier ℝ G
  not_coplanar : ∀ F ∈ faces, ∀ G ∈ faces, F ≠ G → SharesEdge F G →
    ¬ Coplanar ℝ (F ∪ G)
  isConnected : IsConnected (⋃₀ (faces : Set (Set ℝ³)))
  chartedSpace : Nonempty (ChartedSpace ℝ² (⋃₀ (faces : Set (Set ℝ³))))

/-- A polyhedron is *convex* if its surface is the boundary of a convex set. -/
def IsConvexPolyhedron (faces : Finset (Set ℝ³)) : Prop :=
  ∃ K : Set ℝ³, Convex ℝ K ∧ frontier K = ⋃₀ (faces : Set (Set ℝ³))

/-- Sharing an edge is a symmetric relation. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem SharesEdge.symm {F G : Set ℝ³} (h : SharesEdge F G) : SharesEdge G F := by
  obtain ⟨a, b, hab, h⟩ := h
  exact ⟨a, b, hab, Set.inter_comm F G ▸ h⟩

/-- Two faces sharing an edge have nonempty intersection. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem SharesEdge.nonempty_inter {F G : Set ℝ³} (h : SharesEdge F G) : (F ∩ G).Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨a, b, -, h⟩ := h
  exact ⟨a, h (left_mem_segment ℝ a b)⟩

/-- Two faces whose intersection has at most one point do not share an edge. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem not_sharesEdge_of_subsingleton {F G : Set ℝ³} (h : (F ∩ G).Subsingleton) :
    ¬ SharesEdge F G := by
  rintro ⟨a, b, hab, hs⟩
  exact hab (h (hs (left_mem_segment ℝ a b)) (hs (right_mem_segment ℝ a b)))

/-- A polygon is nonempty. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsPolygon.nonempty {F : Set ℝ³} (h : IsPolygon F) : F.Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨-, ⟨e⟩, -⟩ := h
  exact ⟨e.symm ⟨0, Metric.mem_closedBall_self zero_le_one⟩, Subtype.coe_prop _⟩

/-- The empty set is not a polygon. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem not_isPolygon_empty : ¬ IsPolygon (∅ : Set ℝ³) := fun h ↦ by
  simpa using h.nonempty

/--
Is there a non-convex polyhedron without self-intersections with more than seven faces, all of
which share an edge with each other?

Here a polyhedron is a finite set of planar simple polygonal faces forming an embedded closed
surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (`IsPolyhedron`), it is convex if its surface bounds a convex set
(`IsConvexPolyhedron`), and two faces share an edge if their intersection contains a segment of
positive length (`SharesEdge`).

The only known polyhedra all of whose faces are pairwise adjacent are the tetrahedron and the
Szilassi polyhedron. (Non-convexity is automatic for more than seven faces, since Euler's formula
forces such a polyhedron to have positive genus; it is included to match the statement.)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem more_than_seven_faces :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ faces : Finset (Set ℝ³), 7 < faces.card ∧ IsPolyhedron faces ∧
      ¬ IsConvexPolyhedron faces ∧
      ∀ F ∈ faces, ∀ G ∈ faces, F ≠ G → SharesEdge F G := by
  sorry

end MoreThanSevenFaces

items: Polyhedron is modelled set-theoretically: a `Finset (Set ℝ³)` of faces (so the face count is `faces.card`, and injectivity is automatic), rather than a combinatorial map plus vertex coordinates. This sidesteps questions about which points count as vertices (e.g. straight angles / T-junction points) since only the point sets matter.

`IsPolygon F` := `Coplanar ℝ F ∧ Nonempty (F ≃ₜ closedBall (0:ℝ²) 1) ∧ ∃ E : Finset (ℝ³ × ℝ³), intrinsicFrontier ℝ F = ⋃ e ∈ E, segment ℝ e.1 e.2`. A planar set homeomorphic to a closed disk whose relative boundary is a finite union of segments is exactly a (closed) simple polygon region; convexity of faces is deliberately NOT required (the Szilassi polyhedron has non-convex hexagonal faces). Faces with holes are excluded, matching the standard requirement that faces are simple polygons.

'Without self-intersections' is modelled as: (a) distinct faces intersect only inside both relative boundaries (`F ∩ G ⊆ intrinsicFrontier ℝ F ∩ intrinsicFrontier ℝ G`), and (b) the union of the faces is a topological 2-manifold without boundary, expressed as `Nonempty (ChartedSpace ℝ² ↥(⋃₀ ↑faces))` (same convention as `Wikipedia/BingBorsuk.lean`). Together these force every boundary point of a face to be matched by exactly one other face, exclude pinched vertices, triple edges, and touching of far parts of the surface, i.e. the surface is embedded. Compactness is automatic (finite union of disks).

Edge-adjacent faces are required to be non-coplanar (`SharesEdge F G → ¬ Coplanar ℝ (F ∪ G)`). This is not literally in the Wikipedia sentence but is part of what 'face of a polyhedron' means (without it the face count is ill-defined: any face could be subdivided, and planar regions with holes could be simulated by coplanar pieces). Coplanar faces that are disjoint or meet only at a point remain allowed, as usual for non-convex polyhedra. A reviewer should confirm this matches the intended (Szilassi/Grünbaum) notion.
Connectedness of the surface is included in `IsPolyhedron` (a polyhedron is connected); it is redundant given pairwise adjacency but harmless.

'Share an edge' is `SharesEdge F G := ∃ a b, a ≠ b ∧ segment ℝ a b ⊆ F ∩ G` (positive-length common segment, not merely a common vertex), following the decomposition note. Under the manifold + proper-intersection conditions any such segment is contained in a genuine edge of the polyhedron shared by exactly these two faces. T-junctions (a face with a straight angle at a vertex of the polyhedron) are allowed, as they are geometrically legitimate polyhedra.

'Non-convex' is included literally as `¬ IsConvexPolyhedron faces` where `IsConvexPolyhedron faces := ∃ K, Convex ℝ K ∧ frontier K = ⋃₀ ↑faces`. As the decomposition note observes, it is mathematically automatic for more than seven faces (genus ≥ 6), so including it does not change the statement's truth; it is kept to match the text.
Number of faces: strict inequality `7 < faces.card`, matching 'more than seven'. The f = 12, h = 6 remark from the article is not stated separately, following the decomposition table.
AMS tags 51 (geometry) and 52 (convex and discrete geometry) chosen from the problem tags 'geometry, euclidean geometry'.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities: (1) 'polyhedron' is not a Mathlib notion; the final file uses a bespoke embedded-closed-polyhedral-surface definition (planar disk faces, faces meet only along boundaries, adjacent faces non-coplanar, union is a 2-manifold without boundary). 180-degree vertices / T-junctions are allowed, as in Grünbaum-style polyhedra; all three plausible candidates (c04, c07, c08) agree on this. (2) 'Share an edge' is read as a positive-length common segment, per the decomposition notes; candidates requiring the intersection to be exactly one segment (c02, c03, c05, c06) were judged over-restrictive. (3) 'Non-convex' is automatic for >7 pairwise adjacent faces (genus ≥ 2 by Euler's formula) and is included literally as 'the surface is not the frontier of a convex set'. The decomposition note's claim of genus ≥ 6 / f ≡ 0,3,4,7 mod 12 relies on the article's implicit extra assumptions (exactly one shared edge per pair, trivalent vertices); the formalization keeps the literal bound 7 < f, as several candidates correctly pointed out. No candidate omitted the slot.
statement: Is there a non-convex polyhedron without self-intersections with more than seven faces, all of which share an edge with each other?
